I've been working this land for 50 years. I know what this soil wants, what the weather here does, and what my body can manage. My husband and I, just the two of us now — we can't do anything too complicated. I follow what I know works.

All 4.1 mu does both crops. Winter wheat goes in October, comes out June. Then I put maize in right after, comes out by end of September. Same ground, two harvests a year. That's how we've always done it here in Quzhou.

**Wheat:** I'll buy improved seed from the village supply shop — same kind as last year, the local recommended variety. I won't try anything new. Before sowing I'll plough the field like always to break up the maize stubble and loosen the soil. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting — I'll ask the shop owner how much per bag, same as usual. I top-dress with urea in spring at jointing stage. I irrigate three times: once before sowing to wet the seedbed, once in winter to protect roots from frost, once at jointing when the plant is drinking hard. I spray herbicide once in spring and fungicide once if I see powdery mildew coming — last few years I always needed it.

**Maize:** Hybrid seed, no question. Everyone here uses hybrid. I sow it right after wheat harvest, no time to waste. I do rotary tillage — quicker than ploughing, and the soil is already loose enough. I put fertilizer down at planting and top-dress again at the big bell stage. If there's no rain I'll pump from the well — usually two times is enough. I spray once for pests, mostly corn borer.
